analysis: The PR modifies only docs/reference/configuration.md: the visible patch adds two rows near head line 559, documenting DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION. Both are documented as default-on, exact-`0` rollback, forwarded to the launchd provider job. The supplied base units (lines 1-507) contain no changed lines, so the base text was only used for context. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the full second row and any later hunks were not seen. Security relevance: these are memory/cache-management performance controls (MLX buffer-cache sweep, free KV segment retention in paged pools). The documented behavior says retained segments are uncommitted and uncharged, dropped on memory pressure, before load gates and after 30 s idle. Related threats are T-028 (residual GPU memory after requests) and T-029/T-010 (availability and resource monopolization). Retained free KV segments could in theory hold residual KV data longer, which touches T-028. No source code changed here, so I cannot verify whether segments are zeroed or reused only through reinstall, and the docs do not claim they are. The prefix-cache SSD tier (T-041) is not changed. No changes to attestation, authorization (TB-011), encryption or coordinator wire contracts. Remaining integration question: whether the actual code changes behind these docs (GlobalKVCacheBudget.swift, EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift) affect cross-request KV residue in retained segments. They were not supplied and are outside this docs-only unit. Docs-only change; no concrete regression identified.
